name: Matthew
overview: Matthew was a male tax collector who became one of the twelve apostles chosen by YHVH. His calling from a profession often despised in Jewish society highlights the transformative power of Christ's invitation. He is explicitly named as one of the Twelve in Matthew 10:2.
namesAndTitles: The name Matthew means "gift of Yah," reflecting a divine blessing or purpose. This proper name is noted in Matthew 9:9 and does not appear to be given directly by God but holds significant theological meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Matthew's direct relationship with YHVH as both a disciple and an apostle, as stated explicitly in Matthew 10:3. Beyond this, there are no additional family relationships documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Matthew's significance lies in his transition from a tax collector to a devoted follower and apostle of Christ, demonstrating the call of grace to all, regardless of past occupation or status. His inclusion among the twelve apostles underscores his role in spreading the gospel and bearing witness to YHVH's kingdom. His story exemplifies the transformative power of Christ's ministry and the inclusion of diverse individuals in God's plan.
